薩茲琴屬長頸有品魯特琴，音樂學上歸入坦布爾家族；該家族歷史上自伊朗、美索不達米亞: The saz is a long-necked fretted lute, classed in musicology with the tanbur family, which historically spread from Iran and Mesopotamia to Central Asia and Anatolia. In Anatolia the modern saz developed into the main plucked instrument of Turkish folk music and is closely tied to the repertory of the âşık, the itinerant folk poet-singers. In naming, bağlama once mostly meant the smaller sizes, and today it is often linked with the üçtelli cura; in some Alevi traditions a larger dede sazı developed. Larger instruments were once called bozuk, tambura or çöğür, the last seen in Ottoman painting, close in form to the classical tanbur but strung differently. Modern makers often set the frets with a 24-tone equal-temperament calculator and a tuner, so that twelve-tone equal-tempered repertory can be played too.
薩茲琴的琴身通常由桑木或核桃木製成，提供溫暖的音色共鳴。琴頸採用堅硬的梣木或白蠟: The body of the saz is usually mulberry or walnut, which gives a warm resonance. The neck uses a hard ash, for structural stability. The headstock is carved and decorated in red sandalwood or rosewood. The soundboard is spruce or pine. The strings are nylon or steel, in three or four courses. The bridge is bone or hardwood. On traditional instruments the decorated face is inlaid with bone or shell, a mark of Middle Eastern craft.
薩茲琴音色溫暖而富有穿透力，既具有清亮的高音與深沉的低音層次感。其獨特的金屬質感: The saz's timbre is warm and penetrating, with clear high notes and a deep, layered bass. Its distinctive metallic quality comes from the doubled courses: several strings resonating together produce rich overtones and a bleak, poetic sound. The middle register is the fullest, with good sustaining resonance. Compared with the clear brightness of the Western guitar the saz sounds more archaic and hoarse; compared with the Arab oud its high frequencies stand out more and the tone is more biting and forceful. The graininess of the pluck and a subtle percussive sound give it a strong national character. The soundbox makes it project, which suits outdoor performance and the chanting of folk tales.

The saz — bağlama or saz — is a class of long-necked fretted plucked lute, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.321-6 / 321.321. It belongs to the long-necked tanbur family and is common in the folk music of Turkey, Azerbaijan, Armenia, neighbouring parts of the Balkans and western Asia. In Anatolia the modern saz developed into the main lute of Turkish folk music, and it is often played by the âşıks, the itinerant folk poet-singers.
